source_caption_text:
Judge Denied #YellaBeezy’s Request To Kiss His Son Goodbye After He Was Sentenced To Life In Prison 🥺💔

Yella Beezy, Born Markies Deandre Conway, Is A Dallas, Texas Rapper Who Rose To Fame In The Late 2010s With His Breakout Hit “That’s On Me.” Growing Up In Oak Cliff, Dallas, He Built His Name Through His Distinct Southern Flow, Catchy Hooks, And Street-Inspired Storytelling. His Success Helped Put A Bigger Spotlight On The Dallas Hip-Hop Scene, Eventually Leading To Collaborations With Major Artists Including Chris Brown, Quavo, 2 Chainz, And Kevin Gates.

Yella Beezy Continued Building His Career With Popular Tracks Like “Bacc At It Again,” “Up One,” And “Restroom Occupied,” Establishing Himself As One Of The Most Recognizable Rappers Coming Out Of Texas. His Music Earned Millions Of Streams, And He Developed A Loyal Fanbase While Making Appearances Alongside Some Of The Biggest Names In Hip-Hop.

However, His Career Became Overshadowed By A Long-Running Feud With Fellow Dallas Rapper MO3, Born Melvin Abdul Noble Jr. MO3 Was Known For His Emotional Melodies, Powerful Storytelling, And Songs Like “Everybody,” “Broken Love,” And “Outside.” On November 11, 2020, MO3 Was Tragically Sht And Klled On A Dallas Highway At Just 28 Years Old, Leaving The Hip-Hop Community Devastated.
